references.appropriate_for: A response curve with scientifically meaningful breakpoints or thresholds.
references.avoid_when: The x values are unordered categories or interpolation would imply unsupported continuity.
references.structure: One axis, restrained line, breakpoint markers, direct annotations and a meaningful baseline.

references.appropriate_for: Iteration histories where a stopping tolerance or deployment threshold matters.
references.avoid_when: Only the final value exists or the iteration sequence is not comparable.
references.structure: Iteration axis, optional log scale, sparse markers and a labeled stopping threshold.

references.appropriate_for: A small number of comparable series sharing one quantitative scale.
references.avoid_when: Series use incompatible units or color would be the only distinction.
references.structure: Compact publication axes with colorblind-safe colors plus line-style or marker redundancy.

references.appropriate_for: Ordered scenario or method values with a meaningful zero baseline.
references.avoid_when: Zero is not meaningful or uncertainty definitions differ across categories.
references.structure: Sorted bars, direct values, muted context categories and one justified highlight.

references.appropriate_for: Two-objective choices with a defined dominance rule.
references.avoid_when: The candidate set is incomplete without declaring sampling or points are not ordered along the frontier.
references.structure: Candidate points with dominated/non-dominated distinction and only an ordered frontier connected.

references.appropriate_for: A piecewise value function whose active regime changes are central to the claim.
references.avoid_when: Breakpoints are estimated but uncertainty is unavailable or regime labels would crowd the curve.
references.structure: Piecewise line, regime bands, direct breakpoint values and non-overlapping annotations.

references.appropriate_for: Comparing a few distributions on a common measurement scale.
references.avoid_when: Groups have very different sample sizes that are not disclosed or overlap makes shapes unreadable.
references.structure: Common normalization, outline/step density, transparent overlap and explicit sample-size context.

references.appropriate_for: Group distributions where raw observations and median/quartiles are important.
references.avoid_when: Samples are too sparse for density estimation or points would be indecipherably dense.
references.structure: Violin shape, raw points with deterministic jitter and an explicit median or quartile marker.

references.appropriate_for: Paired before/after or matched-condition observations with a real pairing key.
references.avoid_when: Observations are unpaired or connecting lines would imply nonexistent correspondence.
references.structure: Half-density, raw paired points, connecting segments and a compact summary statistic.

references.appropriate_for: Observed paired values with a defensible fit or identity comparison.
references.avoid_when: A fitted line would conceal nonlinear structure or train/test observations are mixed.
references.structure: Visible observations, fit or identity line, uncertainty only when defined and direct outlier annotations.

references.appropriate_for: Predicted-versus-observed performance where marginal distributions expose bias or compression.
references.avoid_when: Predictions are not held out or marginal panels do not add diagnostic evidence.
references.structure: Central identity scatter plus aligned observed and predicted marginal distributions.

references.appropriate_for: A small feature set requiring distribution, pairwise fit and correlation context together.
references.avoid_when: Many features make panels unreadable or multiple-testing implications are ignored.
references.structure: Diagonal distributions, lower/upper pairwise evidence and consistent scales and group colors.

references.appropriate_for: A matrix with explicit row/column semantics and a meaningful color scale.
references.avoid_when: Color values lack a common scale or a diverging midpoint has no scientific meaning.
references.structure: Square matrix, legible cell labels, named colorbar and meaningful sequential or diverging center.

references.appropriate_for: Classification evaluation with genuine held-out folds and defined confidence intervals.
references.avoid_when: Only training predictions exist or copied example AUC values would replace real folds.
references.structure: Light fold curves, dominant mean curve, uncertainty band and dashed chance baseline.

references.appropriate_for: Comparing correlation, standard deviation and centered RMSE for several models.
references.avoid_when: Readers need absolute bias or the three Taylor statistics are not all computed.
references.structure: Polar correlation geometry, reference observation and redundant marker labels for models.

references.appropriate_for: One decision context requiring objective, chosen variables and mechanism to be read together.
references.avoid_when: Panels are unrelated metrics or one relationship already establishes the claim.
references.structure: Two or three aligned panels with shared regimes, direct breakpoint annotations and consistent encoding.

references.appropriate_for: A linked statistical story combining magnitude, distribution and group comparison.
references.avoid_when: Panels use different populations or duplicate the same statistic without adding evidence.
references.structure: Panel labels, shared group colors, raw observations where possible and one conclusion per panel.

references.appropriate_for: Model explanation where global importance and signed sample-level effects are both computed.
references.avoid_when: SHAP values were not computed or feature importance alone answers the claim.
references.structure: Compact global ranking paired with signed effect distribution and consistent feature ordering.

references.appropriate_for: Repeated measurements or estimates with a defined uncertainty interval.
references.avoid_when: The band lacks a documented statistical meaning or independent series are connected as repeated data.
references.structure: Lines differentiated by color and style with restrained uncertainty bands; adapt the official source in network-candidates/seaborn/scripts/errorband_lineplots.py to real data.

references.appropriate_for: A small number of methods compared over the same categories with a meaningful zero baseline.
references.avoid_when: There are many groups, zero is irrelevant, or uncertainty definitions differ.
references.structure: Grouped bars with defined error bars, direct values where useful, and added hatch patterns for grayscale.

references.appropriate_for: Comparing distributions across two categorical factors.
references.avoid_when: Samples are too sparse or raw observations are necessary to expose structure.
references.structure: Grouped boxes on a common scale with sample sizes and raw observations added when affordable.

references.appropriate_for: Many categories with long labels and comparable numeric distributions.
references.avoid_when: Ordering has no meaning or outliers are hidden without explanation.
references.structure: Horizontal boxes sorted by a declared statistic with explicit outlier semantics.

references.appropriate_for: Two quantitative axes plus a defensible positive magnitude encoded by area.
references.avoid_when: Bubble size represents signed values, precise size comparison is required, or points heavily overlap.
references.structure: Perceptually scaled bubble area with marker redundancy for categories and sparse direct annotation.

references.appropriate_for: Showing how a few groups contribute to counts across common bins.
references.avoid_when: Group shapes must be compared precisely or bin choice would dominate the conclusion.
references.structure: Common declared bins and normalization with sample-size disclosure and grayscale-safe group distinction.

references.appropriate_for: Comparing complete distributions without choosing histogram bins.
references.avoid_when: There are too many groups or weighted observations are not handled explicitly.
references.structure: Step curves with color plus line-style redundancy and direct decision-relevant quantiles.

references.appropriate_for: Checking systematic residual structure, heteroscedasticity, and outliers after fitting.
references.avoid_when: Residuals are computed on training data only or their sign convention is unstated.
references.structure: Held-out residual points around a labeled zero baseline with stated residual definition and scale.

references.appropriate_for: A compact matrix with meaningful row and column labels and a common scale.
references.avoid_when: Cells are not comparable or a diverging midpoint has no scientific interpretation.
references.structure: Semantic colormap, labeled colorbar, controlled annotation density, and readable row/column labels.

references.appropriate_for: Matched observations across ordered conditions with a real pairing key.
references.avoid_when: Observations are independent or connecting lines imply nonexistent correspondence.
references.structure: Individual paired paths separated from aggregate estimates, preserving real pairing IDs.

references.appropriate_for: A few aligned time series sharing units and sampling times.
references.avoid_when: Series use different units or dense lines obscure the decision-relevant trend.
references.structure: Compact aligned series with direct labels or a small legend and line-style redundancy.

references.appropriate_for: Comparing component values against explicit totals across categories.
references.avoid_when: Components do not share a common whole or totals vary without being shown.
references.structure: Deliberately sorted horizontal totals and components with a stated denominator and direct differences.
